washington-university-in-st-louis.faculty: Philip H. Dybvig, who won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences (with Ben Bernanke and Douglas Diamond) for research on banks and financial crises, is current faculty at WashU's Olin Business School, where he has taught since 1990. (Faculty change — verify.)

university-of-southern-california.faculty: Arieh Warshel, a Distinguished Professor of Chemistry at USC Dornsife, won the 2013 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing multiscale models for complex chemical systems. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.undergrad: Nearly all students engage through the Summer Research Program, faculty-led projects, independent research, and the SCOPE capstone, where teams complete sponsored engineering projects for outside companies.
research.areas: Human-centered engineering, robotics and automation, engineering education/pedagogy, assistive technology, and sustainability (including autonomous farming systems).

research.undergrad: Students work closely with faculty mentors from early in their time at Pitzer, including through NSF-funded Research Opportunities for Undergraduates (REU) and paid summer fellowships such as the JF Harmon Faculty-Student Research Assistantship Program.
research.areas: Community-engaged and applied research through centers including the Global Mental Health Lab, the Robert Redford Conservancy for environmental sustainability, and the Firestone Center for Restoration Ecology (a field station in Costa Rica).

georgetown-university.faculty: George Akerlof, who shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for work on markets with asymmetric information, is University Professor at Georgetown, with an appointment in the Economics Department and the McCourt School of Public Policy. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.undergrad: Undergraduates work in faculty labs and on funded projects, e.g. through research fellowships and centers-based work; Georgetown highlights students collaborating directly with faculty such as in multiple-sclerosis research.
research.areas: Interdisciplinary strengths in health and biomedical research, environmental sustainability (Earth Commons Institute), and technology and society.

research.undergrad: Undergraduates work alongside faculty as research colleagues, presenting at national conferences and co-authoring papers; the Albert Nerken School of Engineering partners with outside institutions including Memorial Sloan Kettering and the Simons Foundation Flatiron Institute.
research.areas: Bioengineering, autonomous and cyber-physical systems, machine learning/data science, and sustainability, funded by NSF, NIH, and NIST grants.

research.undergrad: About 120 students a year receive Summer Research Program grants across all disciplines; the Senior Fellowship Program lets select seniors devote their whole final year to an original research project, and an International Summer Research Fellowship supports research abroad.
research.areas: Student work spans biology (small-mammal/reforestation studies), psychology, economics (with the Griffiss Institute), computer science, and neuroscience, often leading to publication or conference presentation.

research.undergrad: Davidson funds semester-long and summer independent research through Student Research Opportunities grants and the Davidson Research Initiative (DRI), with summer support from sources including the Duke Endowment and Howard Hughes Medical Institute; over 60% of faculty publish with undergraduate co-authors.
research.areas: Research spans biology, chemistry, physics, environmental studies, history, and political science, supported by the Baker-Watt Science Complex.

boston-university.faculty: Sheldon Glashow, who shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for work unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces, holds an active title as Metcalf Professor of Mathematics and Physics at Boston University (in addition to emeritus status at Harvard). (Faculty change — verify.)

research.level: R1 (Carnegie Classification); one of 71 AAU member universities
research.areas: Biomedical engineering and health sciences (including the Framingham Heart Study Brain Aging Program), infectious diseases, computing/data sciences, and materials science, with $574 million in FY25 research awards.

new-york-university.faculty: Thomas J. Sargent, who shared the 2011 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for empirical research on cause and effect in the macroeconomy, is the W.R. Berkley Professor of Economics and Business at NYU Stern (on faculty since 2002). Hong Wang, a Courant Institute mathematician who (with Joshua Zahl) proved the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, was awarded the 2026 Fields Medal — she became a full professor at NYU in September 2025, though she holds that post jointly with a permanent professorship at IHES in France. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.areas: Strengths in mathematics (Courant Institute), biomedical research (cancer and heart-disease prediction tools), and artificial intelligence, with a strong undergraduate research office.

research.level: AAU member; top-tier research institution (ranked among top 100 U.S. patent-earning universities)
research.undergrad: Roughly half of Notre Dame undergraduates participate in original research, supported across more than thirty core facilities.
research.areas: Health and well-being, environmental sustainability, AI and advanced computation, and engineering/physics — Notre Dame physicists contributed to the CMS experiment's Higgs boson discovery at CERN.

Two UVA faculty — Scott C. Doney (environmental sciences) and Raymond E. Keller (biology) — were elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2025, reflecting strength in environmental and developmental biology research.

university-of-north-carolina-at-chapel-h.faculty: Aziz Sancar, who won the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for mapping DNA repair mechanisms, remains an active UNC School of Medicine professor (Sarah Graham Kenan Professor of Biochemistry and Biophysics), still teaching and running his lab as of late 2025. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.level: Top-tier research institution; ~$1.6B in annual sponsored research from all sources
research.areas: Strategic priorities include AI applied to medicine, disease prevention/cure, environmental and renewable solutions, and brain health.

boston-college.faculty: Paul Romer, who shared the 2018 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for integrating technological innovation into long-run macroeconomic analysis, joined Boston College's Carroll School of Management as the Seidner University Professor in fall 2023. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.areas: Economics and policy (retirement security, income mobility), quantum materials and glaciology, and the new Schiller Institute for Integrated Science and Society.

northeastern-university.faculty: Albert-László Barabási, University Distinguished Professor and Robert Gray Dodge Professor of Network Science, pioneered the discovery of scale-free networks and the Barabási–Albert model; he was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2024. (Faculty change — verify.)
